- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >50% negative values) and model forecasts remain flat or upward, adjust downward by 2–5% to account for bearish sentiment bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 periods to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk — add 3–7% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change 1–2 periods ahead.  
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive declines), reduce forecast slope by 15–30% to align with mean-reversion behavior.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overestimate volatility — cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day average to avoid overreaction.
